related_questions.question: How do I check my UK ETA status?

text_blocks.snippet: To check the status of your UK Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) application, you should first check your email for a decision from UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI), which usually arrives within 3 working days. If you haven't received an email or if it's been longer than 3 working days, you can visit the official GOV.UK website for guidance or contact UKVI directly.
snippet_highlighted_words: check your email for a decision from UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI)

list.title: 1. Check your email:
list.snippet: The UKVI will send you an email with a decision on your ETA application. This email will also contain your 16-digit ETA reference number.

list.title: 2. Check the official website:
list.snippet: If you haven't received an email or need further information, go to the official GOV.UK website for guidance and to potentially check your status online.

list.title: 3. Contact UKVI:
list.snippet: If you're still unsure or need further assistance, you can contact UK Visas and Immigration for support.

list.title: 4. Consider the ETA app:
list.snippet: If you applied using the UK ETA app, the app will be linked to your passport, and you don't need to show anything else when entering the UK.

related_questions.question: What is needed to enter the UK from the USA?

text_blocks.snippet: U.S. citizens traveling to the UK need an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) if they don't have a UK visa or legal residency. The ETA acts as a pre-clearance for travel and is required for all parts of the UK, including Northern Ireland. You can apply for an ETA online through the UK government website.
snippet_highlighted_words: an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) if they don't have a UK visa or legal residency

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a breakdown of what's needed:

list.snippet: Valid Passport: Your passport must be valid for the entire duration of your stay.
Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA): Most U.S. citizens will need an ETA to enter the UK, which is obtained online.
Visa (if applicable): If your visit is for longer than 6 months, or for purposes other than tourism or short business trips, you may need a visa.
Proof of Funds: You may need to demonstrate you have sufficient funds to support yourself during your stay.
Return Ticket: You may need to show proof of onward travel, such as a return ticket.
ETA Application: You can apply for the ETA online through the official UK government website. The application includes providing personal details, passport information, and answering a few questions.
ETA Fee: The ETA costs £10 (around $13 USD) per person.

related_questions.question: How do I check my UK visa status?

text_blocks.snippet: To check your UK visa application status, you can track your application online through VFS Global or, if you have an eVisa, by accessing your UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) account. You'll need your application reference number (usually on your receipt) and your last name to track online. If you've set up an account, you can also use the "View and Prove" service to check your status.
Here's a breakdown of the methods:

list.snippet: Go to the VFS Global website.
Select your Visa Application Centre (VAC) if prompted.
Navigate to the "Track Your Application" section.
Enter your application reference number (often a GWF number) and your last name.
Submit the information to view the current status of your application.

text_blocks.snippet: 2. Checking Online Through Your UKVI Account (if applicable):

list.snippet: Visit the GOV.UK website and navigate to the "View and Prove" service.
Sign in using your UKVI account details.
You can then view your eVisa and check your current immigration status.
If you need further assistance, you can contact UKVI directly.
You can find contact information on the GOV.UK website.
Be aware that they can provide updates on the progress of your application but may not offer personalized advice.
